source: UK Full Business Case (Five Case Model) - Track-1 CCUS Cluster Sequencing

risks.description: There is a risk that government (HMG) is exposed to increased costs for Track-1 post-Financial Investment Decision (FID), and that cost pressures are unaffordable within delegated budgets. [Strategic Case risk T1SR1, Section 2.5 'Identify high level potential risks', p.20-21; source rating: High/Possible.]
risks.mitigation: Contractual mechanisms ensure HMG only takes on specific risks where appropriate, with liability limited and counterparties incentivised to control costs; governance mechanisms monitor costs and provide early warning of overruns; contingent liability exposure is accurately monitored.

risks.description: There is a risk that the programme does not realise its intended benefits for Track-1. [Strategic Case risk T1SR3, Section 2.5, p.20-21; source rating: High/Possible.]
risks.mitigation: Projects undergo detailed technical assurance and financial due diligence; projects must meet Initial Conditions Precedent (ICPs) before contracts take effect and Operational CPs thereafter, with LCCC able to terminate and avoid paying for an underperforming project; contractual mechanisms allocate performance-related risk to the private sector; continued engagement with the global Carbon Management Challenge to expand CCUS use and deliver UK trade benefits.

risks.description: There is a risk that the post-FID operating model across public and private sector parties will not operate successfully. [Strategic Case risk T1SR4, Section 2.5, p.20-21; source rating: Medium/Possible.]
risks.mitigation: Progress of arm's-length bodies' (ALBs') capacity (funding, resource) and capability (knowledge, skills) to operate successfully post-FID is monitored through the Delivery Board; a DESNZ Cluster Sponsor Function will be set up between FID and Commercial Operations Date (COD) to mitigate risks to cluster delivery and system integration; readiness-testing mechanisms are in place ahead of FID; FY24/25 funding for the ALBs to fulfil their roles has been secured.

risks.description: There is a risk of an unclear exit path for HMG from its role in the Track-1 commercial framework. [Strategic Case risk T1SR5, Section 2.5, p.20-21; source rating: High/Possible.]
risks.mitigation: Key planned developments include amendments to the process for granting economic licences, a move toward a competitive allocation process for capture contracts, and evolution of transport & storage business models to reflect an increased private-sector role in managing cross-chain risks; cost-reduction levers (UK ETS pricing, CBAMs) are intended to help cultivate a self-sustaining industry and enable an HMG exit path.

STRUCTURE (unchanged from prior note): UK Five Case Model business cases scatter risk content across multiple sections rather than one consolidated section like WB's SORT table + Key Risks, in incompatible framings (narrative, rated table, quantitative NPV sensitivity).

METHODOLOGY (2026-07-19 decision, unchanged): ground truth = ONLY the single closest structural analog to a WB SORT-table register, which for this document is Sec 2.5 (now pp.20-21). All other risk-bearing sections listed above are excised from model-facing planning text for leakage safety but are not scored against.

RATING CONVENTION (unchanged): the source gives each Sec 2.5 risk a combined qualitative rating (e.g. 'High/Possible') rather than WB's single SORT ordinal. Read as Impact/Likelihood per the standard UK government 5x5 risk-matrix convention (Likelihood: Rare=1, Unlikely=2, Possible=3, Likely=4, Almost Certain=5; Impact: Negligible=1, Low=2, Medium=3, High=4, Very High=5). The qualitative terms are verbatim from the source; the specific 1-5 integers are this project's interpretive mapping, not numbers stated by the source, and should be checked by a second rater before use.
